name: Industrial Boiler- Coal
notes:
The emission factors in g/mmBtu are calculated based on those for coal-fired utility boilers in g/kWh and the electricity generation efficiencies.

Reference: Hao Cai, Michael Wang, Amgad Elgowainy, Jeongwoo Han. Updated Greenhouse Gas and Criteria Air Pollutant Emission Factors of the U.S. Electric Generating Units in 2010. October 25, 2013. https://greet.es.anl.gov/publication-electricity-13

name: Central Plants G.H2 Production from Coal with CO2 Balance
notes:
This technology is created to account the emissions used in the G.H2 central plant production processes, in which these emission items are defined at per mmbtu G.H2 produced.  Because the process efficiencies vary from year to year and from with co-product to without co-product, and because we assumed any feedstock beyond the 1mmbtu in the feed is counted as feed loss, we can define this technology in such a way that as long as it is applied to 1mmbtu feed (which together with the process fuels produces the 1mmbtu G.H2), the emissions will be calculated as constants per 1mmbtu G.H2 production.

There are three scenarios for G.H2 production from coal:
For scenario 1, the non-combustion emissions from coking plant (see details in GREET2.7) are allocated between output coke, COG and other by-products.
For scenario 2 and 3, there are no non-combustion emissions.
